rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is wise: He does only what His wisdom requires.
rows.anchor: الذي لا يفعل إلا ما تستدعيه حكمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanation of the heavens made without visible pillars was given earlier in Sūrat al-Raʿd.
rows.anchor: خلق السموات بغير عمد ترونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains are lofty and fixed to keep the earth from swaying; its similar parts would otherwise shift positions, since none is inherently tied to one place.
rows.anchor: كراهة أن تميد بكم، فإن تشابه أجزائها يقتضي تبدل أحيازها وأوضاعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God spread every kind of creature through the earth.
rows.anchor: وبث فيها من كل دابة

words: وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءًۭ فَأَنۢبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍۢ كَرِيمٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A noble kind is a species abundant in benefit; the rain produces such kinds of plants.
rows.anchor: من كل صنف كثير المنفعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These signs demonstrate God's might, the perfection of His power, and His wisdom, the perfection of His knowledge; they prepare and establish the doctrine of divine oneness.
rows.anchor: وكأنه استدل بذلك على عزته التي هي كمال القدرة، وحكمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The things just described are God's creation; the challenge asks what the alleged gods created to deserve sharing in His divinity.
rows.anchor: هذا الذي ذكر مخلوقه فماذا خلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayḍāwī parses mādhā either as the object of khalaqa, or as mā in the subject position with dhā and its relative clause as predicate; fa-arūnī is suspended by the question.
rows.anchor: ماذا } نصب ب { خلق } أو ما مرتفع بالابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse turns from rebuking the idolaters to declaring their unmistakable error; naming them as wrongdoers in place of a pronoun signals that shirk is injustice.
rows.anchor: إضراب عن تبكيتهم إلى التسجيل عليهم بالضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their enjoyment is little either in amount or duration, because what passes away is little beside what lasts.
rows.anchor: تمتيعا أو زمانا قليلا فإن ما يزول بالنسبة إلى ما يدوم قليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The severe punishment weighs on them like massive bodies, or combines burning with constriction.
rows.anchor: أو يضم إلى الإحراق الضغط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proof that no one besides God can create is so clear that the idolaters are compelled to admit He created the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: لوضوح الدليل المانع من إسناد الخلق إلى غيره بحيث اضطروا إلى إذاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to praise God follows because their forced admission proves their own belief false.
rows.anchor: على إلزامهم والجائهم إلى الإعتراف بما يوجب بطلان معتقدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most fail to understand what their admission logically entails.
rows.anchor: لا يعلمون } أن ذلك يلزمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because everything in the heavens and earth belongs to God, no other being there deserves worship.
rows.anchor: لا يستحق العبادة فيهما غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God needs no praise from those who praise Him, yet deserves praise whether or not anyone praises Him.
rows.anchor: عن حمد الحامدين. { الحميد } المستحق للحمد وإن لم يحمد

words: وَلَوْ أَنَّمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مِن شَجَرَةٍ أَقْلَٰمٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypothetical makes every individual tree a pen; the singular shajara is used while distributing the claim across individual trees.
rows.anchor: ولو ثبت كون الأشجار أقلاما، وتوحيد { شجرة } لأن المراد

words: وَٱلْبَحْرُ يَمُدُّهُۥ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦ سَبْعَةُ أَبْحُرٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vast surrounding sea is extended with seven more seas as ink; madduhu conveys supplying the ink, as when one extends an inkpot.
rows.anchor: والبحر المحيط بسعته مدادا ممدودا بسبعة أبحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayḍāwī gives several parses: raising the sea by coordination with the clause after anna, as a new subject, or as a circumstantial clause; the Basrans also allow accusative coordination or an implied verb explained by yamudduhu.
rows.anchor: ورفعه للعطف على محل أن ومعموليها وبمده حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage is also read tamudduhu or yamudduhu, with feminine tāʾ or masculine yāʾ.
rows.anchor: «تمده» «ويمده» بالياء والتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even writing God's words with all those pens and seas would not exhaust them; the plural of paucity emphasizes that the resources cannot suffice even for a little, much less much.
rows.anchor: بكتبها بتلك الأقلام بذلك المداد وإيثار جمع القلة للإشعار بأن ذلك لا يفي بالقليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is invincible, and nothing falls outside His knowledge and wisdom.
rows.anchor: حكيم } لا يخرج عن علمه وحكمته أمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayḍāwī says the verse answers Jews who asked the Prophet, or instructed Quraysh envoys to ask him, about the statement that people were given little knowledge; they said the Torah contains knowledge of everything.
rows.anchor: والآية جواب لليهود سألوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أو أمروا وفد قريش

words: مَا خَلْقُكُمْ وَلَا بَعْثُكُمْ إِلَّا كَنَفْسٍ وَٰحِدَةٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creating and resurrecting all people is like doing so for one person: God's will and inherent power suffice for everything, and one task does not distract Him from another.
rows.anchor: إلا كخلقها وبعثها إذ لا يشغله شأن عن شأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears and sees every object of perception; perceiving one does not distract Him from perceiving another, just as creating one does not.
rows.anchor: يسمع كل مسموع { بصير } يبصر كل مبصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angel takes all of your souls and leaves none of you behind; tafaʿʿala and istafʿala often converge in meaning, as in the paired verbs he cites.
rows.anchor: يستوفي نفوسكم لا يترك منها شيئا ولا يبقي منكم أحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Angel of Death is assigned to take people's souls and keep count of their appointed lifespans.
rows.anchor: بقبض أرواحكم وإحصاء آجالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People return to their Lord for judgment and recompense.
rows.anchor: للحساب والجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guilty lower their heads from shame and humiliation before their Lord.
rows.anchor: من الحياء والخزي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say they have seen what was promised and heard their Lord confirm His messengers; they ask to return to worldly life and act righteously because what they witnessed has removed doubt.
rows.anchor: إذ لم يبق لنا شك بما شاهدنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer to law is omitted, understood as “you would see something dreadful”; alternatively, law expresses a wish, with past tense in law and idh because what is certain in God's knowledge is like what has happened.
rows.anchor: وجواب { لو } محذوف تقديره لرأيت أمرا فظيعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tarā needs no expressed object when it means seeing at that time; alternatively its object is supplied by what follows idh, and the address may be to the Prophet or anyone.
rows.anchor: ولا يقدر ل { ترى } مفعول لأن المعنى لو يكون منك رؤية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nearer punishment is worldly affliction: the seven-year drought, killing, and captivity they endured.
rows.anchor: عذاب الدنيا يريد ما محنوا به من السنة سبع سنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greater punishment is the punishment of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: دون العذاب الاكبر } عذاب الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hope of return concerns those who survive the worldly punishment, so that they may repent of disbelief.
rows.anchor: يتوبون عن الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says al-Walīd ibn ʿUqba vied with ʿAlī at Badr, and these verses were revealed.
rows.anchor: روي أن الوليد ابن عقبة فاخر عليا رضي الله عنه يوم بدر فنزلت هذه الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning away means failing to reflect on the signs; thumma marks how astonishing it is to reject clear guidance to happiness after rational reminder, as the cited Hamāsa verse illustrates.
rows.anchor: فلم يتفكر فيها، و { ثم } لاستبعاد الإعراض عنها مع فرض وضوحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hamāsa verse likens inexplicable rejection to a free man who sees death's waves and then walks into them, underscoring the strangeness of turning from manifest signs.
rows.anchor: ولا يكشف الغماء إلا ابن حرة يرى غمرات الموت ثم يزورها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God takes vengeance on criminals, how much more will He take vengeance on the one more unjust than every wrongdoer.
rows.anchor: فكيف ممن كان أظلم من كل ظالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave Moses the Scripture just as He gave it to Muhammad; the latter's reception is not unprecedented, as the Qur'an says that he receives the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: ءاتينا موسى الكتب } كما آتيناك

words: فَلَا تَكُن فِى مِرْيَةٍۢ مِّن لِّقَآئِهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may mean no doubt about receiving the Scripture as Moses did, Moses meeting the Scripture, or Muhammad meeting Moses.
rows.anchor: أو من لقاء موسى للكتاب أو من لقائك موسى

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said that on the Night Journey he saw Moses, a tall, brown-skinned man with curly hair, resembling a man of the Shanu'a.
rows.anchor: موسى. وعنه عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhālikum points either to all that was just mentioned or to the last item.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى ما ذكر أو إلى الأخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A claim made only by your mouths has no reality in the world, like a madman's babbling; God's speech is true and corresponds to objective reality.
rows.anchor: لا حقيقة له في الأعيان كقول الهاذي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guides the path of truth.
rows.anchor: سبيل الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Name adopted children after their fathers; this is the relevant part of the statements of truth mentioned above.
rows.anchor: أنسبوهم إليهم، وهو أفراد للمقصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the act of naming them after their fathers; aqsaṭ justifies that instruction, and the comparative form means greater truthfulness in an absolute sense.
rows.anchor: هو أقسط عند الله } تعليل له، والضمير لمصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If their fathers are unknown, regard them as brothers in religion and allies, calling someone “my brother” or “my ally” in that sense.
rows.anchor: وأولياؤكم فيه فقولوا هذا أخي ومولاي بهذا التأويل

words: وَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌۭ فِيمَآ أَخْطَأْتُم بِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no sin for mistaken attribution before the prohibition or later through forgetfulness or a slip of the tongue; liability attaches to what hearts intend.
rows.anchor: مخطئين قبل النهي أو بعده على النسيان أو سبق اللسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted sense is either that sin attaches to what hearts deliberately intend, or that deliberate intention itself bears the sin.
rows.anchor: ولكن الجناح فيما تعمدت قلوبكم أو ولكن ما تعمدت قلوبكم فيه الجناح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is forgiving and merciful because He pardons the person who makes a mistake.
rows.anchor: لعفوه عن المخطىء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Bayḍāwī's school adoption has no legal effect; Abū Ḥanīfa holds that adopting a slave emancipates him and establishes lineage for an unknown child who could be attached to the adopter.
rows.anchor: أن التبني لا عبرة به عندنا وعند أبي حنيفة

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa holds that adoption can establish the lineage of an unknown child if the child could be affiliated with the adopter.
rows.anchor: وعند أبي حنيفة يوجب عتق مملوكه ويثبت النسب لمجهوله

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ وَمَلَٰٓئِكَتَهُۥ يُصَلُّونَ عَلَى ٱلنَّبِىِّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God and His angels show the Prophet's honor and magnify his rank.
rows.anchor: يعتنون بإظهار شرفه وتعظيم شأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should likewise show him care, saying, “O God, bless Muhammad.”
rows.anchor: اعتنوا أنتم أيضا فإنكم أولى بذلك وقولوا اللهم صل على محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taslim may mean saying the greeting “Peace be upon you, Prophet,” or submitting to the Prophet's commands.
rows.anchor: وقولوا السلام عليك أيها النبي وقيل وانقادوا لأوامره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes that invoking blessing and peace upon the Prophet is obligatory at least in general.
rows.anchor: والآية تدل على وجوب الصلاة والسلام عليه في الجملة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view makes invoking blessing obligatory every time the Prophet is mentioned.
rows.anchor: وقيل تجب الصلاة كلما جرى ذكره

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report condemns the person who hears the Prophet mentioned but fails to invoke blessing upon him.
rows.anchor:
عليه الصلاة والسلام
" رغم أنف رجل ذكرت عنده فلم يصل علي "

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Another Prophetic report prays that a person who hears the Prophet mentioned, fails to invoke blessing, and enters Hell be cast far away.
rows.anchor:
عليه الصلاة والسلام
" رغم أنف رجل ذكرت عنده فلم يصل علي "
وقوله
" من ذكرت عنده فلم يصل علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blessing on another person is permitted when attached to the Prophet's blessing, but disliked by itself because custom has made it a distinctive formula for mentioning the Messenger.
rows.anchor: على غيره تبعا. وتكره استقلالا لأنه في العرف صار شعارا لذكر الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the same customary reason, it is disliked to call Muhammad “mighty and majestic,” although those descriptions are true of him.
rows.anchor: ولذلك كره أن يقال محمد عز وجل وإن كان عزيزا وجليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They offend God by acts He dislikes, such as disbelief and sins; alternatively, they offend the Messenger by breaking his tooth or calling him a poet or madman.
rows.anchor: أو يؤذون رسول الله بكسر رباعيته وقولهم شاعر مجنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is mentioned in the phrase to magnify Him; those who allow one expression to bear two senses can understand both senses according to its two objects.
rows.anchor: وذكر الله للتعظيم له. ومن جوز إطلاق اللفظ على معنيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's curse means that He removes them from His mercy.
rows.anchor: أبعدهم من رحمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment humiliates them while also causing pain.
rows.anchor: يهينهم مع الإيلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question establishes the point also made in 19:87: the false gods have no power over intercession.
rows.anchor: يريد به تقرير قوله لا يملكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no other possible answer; silence or hesitation from fear of the implication still signals inward acknowledgment.
rows.anchor: إذ لا جواب سواه، وفيه إشعار بأنهم إن سكتوا أو تلعثموا في الجواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the preceding proof identifies the guided and the astray, the wording pretends to fairness—“we or you”—and silences a quarrelsome opponent more effectively than direct accusation; it is not real uncertainty.
rows.anchor: وهو بعد ما تقدم من التقرير البليغ الدال على من هو على الهدى

words: لَعَلَىٰ هُدًى أَوْ فِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two groups are monotheists who worship the sole giver of provision and possessor of intrinsic power, and idolaters who associate lowly inanimate beings with Him.
rows.anchor: والمشركين به الجماد النازل في أدنى المراتب الإمكانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poet Ḥassān offers a parallel in which a seemingly evenhanded question carries a pointed rebuke: “Which of you is the lesser, let the better of you be ransomed.”
rows.anchor:
ونظيره قول حسان:
أتهجوه ولست له بكفء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition ʿalā evokes a guided person above a minaret surveying things or riding a horse he can direct.
rows.anchor: لأن الهادي كمن صعد منارا ينظر الأشياء ويتطلع عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition fī evokes a lost person immersed in darkness and confusion, or confined in a pit with no escape.
rows.anchor: والضال كأنه منغمس في ظلام مرتبك لا يرى شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appointed term may be the duration of the sun and moon's cycle, their endpoint, or the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: هي مدة دوره أو منتهاه أو يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhālikum points to the agent responsible for the preceding cosmic actions; His agency underpins the repeated affirmations that follow.
rows.anchor: الإشارة إلى الفاعل لهذه الأشياء. وفيها إشعار بأن فاعليته لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause “to Him belongs sovereignty” may instead begin a new statement in the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون { له الملك } كلاما مبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idols own not even a date-pit's thin covering; this demonstrates God's exclusive divinity and lordship.
rows.anchor: للدلالة على تفرده بالألوهية والربوبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols are inanimate and cannot hear their worshippers.
rows.anchor: لأنهم جماد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if they could hear, they could not benefit the worshippers; alternatively, they would disown them and their worship.
rows.anchor: أو لتبرئهم منكم مما تدعون لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day the idols will acknowledge the falsity of the association, or say, “You were not worshipping us.”
rows.anchor: بإشراككم لهم يقرون ببطلانه أو يقولون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No informer matches the truly knowledgeable God; the verse confirms His account of the idols and refutes the claims made for them.
rows.anchor: فإنه الخبير به على الحقيقة دون سائر المخبرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People need God in their very selves and in everything that befalls them; the definite plural intensifies their dependence, which is so great that other creatures' need scarcely counts by comparison.
rows.anchor: وتعريف الفقراء للمبالغة في فقرهم كأنهم لشدة افتقارهم وكثرة احتياجهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is absolutely self-sufficient and benefits all beings, so He deserves their praise.
rows.anchor: المستغني على الإطلاق المنعم على سائر الموجودات حتى استحق عليهم الحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could remove humankind and replace it with a more obedient people, or with an entirely different world.
rows.anchor: أو بعالم آخر غير ما تعرفونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing of this is impossible or difficult for God.
rows.anchor: بمتعذر أو متعسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No sinful soul carries another's sin; 29:13 does not contradict this, since misleaders carry their own sin of misleading in addition to their own misguidance, not someone else's burden.
rows.anchor: فإنهم يحملون أثقال إضلالهم مع أثقال ضلالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A muthqala is a soul weighed down by sins.
rows.anchor: نفس أثقلها الأوزار

words: إِلَىٰ حَمْلِهَا لَا يُحْمَلْ مِنْهُ شَىْءٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one accepts a share of another's burden: the verse denies that another's sin can be borne on a soul's behalf, just as it denies that the soul bears another's sin.
rows.anchor: نفى أن يحمل عنها ذنبها كما نفى أن يحمل عليها ذنب غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The called-on helper is omitted because it is implied by in tadʿu; the reading dhū qurbā supplies an omitted predicate and is preferable to treating kāna as a complete verb, which does not fit the syntax.
rows.anchor: فأضمر المدعو لدلالة إن تدع عليه.

words: إِنَّمَا تُنذِرُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلْغَيْبِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning benefits those who fear their Lord unseen: either they fear the absent punishment, fear while alone, or the punishment is absent from them.
rows.anchor: غائبين عن عذابه، أو عن الناس في خلواتهم، أو غائبا عنهم عذابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who establish prayer, along with those who fear God, are the ones who benefit from warning; the differing verb forms reflect ongoing practice.
rows.anchor: واختلاف الفعلين لما مر من الاستمرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To purify oneself is to cleanse oneself of the stain of sins; that purification benefits the person alone.
rows.anchor: ومن تطهر من دنس المعاصي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading is man azkā fa-innamā yazzakkā; the inserted clause reinforces that fear of God and establishing prayer are themselves forms of purification.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «ومن أزكى فإنما يزكي» وهو اعتراض مؤكد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone returns to God, who recompenses them for their purification.
rows.anchor: فيجازيهم على تزكيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two envoys were Yaḥyā and Yūnus, according to one identification.
rows.anchor: وهما يحيى ويونس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the two envoys were people other than Yaḥyā and Yūnus.
rows.anchor: وقيل غيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-ʿazzaznā means “We strengthened.”
rows.anchor: فكذبوهما فعززنا } فقوينا

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abū Bakr reads the verb without doubling, from ʿazzahu meaning “he overcame him”; its object is omitted because the preceding context supplies it and the helper is the focus.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر مخففا من عزه إذا غلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third envoy was Simon.
rows.anchor: ذكر المعزز به. { بثالث } وهو شمعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people worshipped idols; Jesus sent two envoys, who met Ḥabīb al-Najjār tending sheep. They healed his sick son, and many others were healed, so the news reached the king.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنهم كانوا عبدة أصنام فأرسل إليهم عيسى عليه السلام اثنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the king asked whether another god existed, the envoys named the creator of the king and his idols. The king imprisoned them, and Jesus sent Simon, who entered in disguise and befriended the court and king.
rows.anchor: ثم بعث عيسى شمعون فدخل متنكرا وعاشر أصحاب الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Simon arranged for the envoys to answer the king, who asked for signs; they prayed for a blind boy and his sight was restored, then challenged the idols to do the same.
rows.anchor: الله الذي خلق كل شيء وليس له شريك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king admitted that the idols neither hear nor see nor harm nor benefit. He then demanded resurrection; the envoys prayed, and a boy dead for seven days rose and warned the people of the seven valleys of Fire.
rows.anchor: آلهتنا لا تسمع ولا تبصر ولا تضر ولا تنفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revived boy said he saw a handsome young man in heaven interceding for the three envoys; the king recognized Simon and the two others.
rows.anchor: فرأيت شابا حسنا يشفع لهؤلاء الثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Simon saw that his words had affected the king and urged him; the king and a group believed, while Gabriel cried out against the unbelievers and they perished.
rows.anchor: ومن لم يؤمن صاح عليهم جبريل عليه الصلاة والسلام فهلكوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people object that the messengers are ordinary humans with no distinction that would qualify them for their claimed privilege.
rows.anchor: لا مزية لكم علينا تقتضي اختصاصكم بما تدعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bashar is nominative because the particle mā loses its governing effect before illā.
rows.anchor: ورفع بشر لانتقاض النفي المقتضي إعمال ما بإلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They mean that God sent down no revelation or message.
rows.anchor: وحي ورسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They accuse the envoys of lying about their mission.
rows.anchor: في دعوى الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The envoys invoke God's knowledge, which functions like an oath, and add the emphatic lām in reply to the people's denial.
rows.anchor: استشهدوا بعلم الله وهو يجري مجرى القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their only duty is clear, manifest delivery, made plain by signs that demonstrate the truth of the message.
rows.anchor: الظاهر البين بالآيات الشاهدة لصحته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people say they take the envoys as an ill omen because the message seems strange, offensive, and repellent to them.
rows.anchor: تشاءمنا بكم، وذلك لاستغرابهم ما ادعوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They threaten to stone the envoys and inflict painful punishment unless they stop their preaching.
rows.anchor: عن مقالتكم هذه. { لنرجمنكم وليمسنكم منا عذاب أليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their ill fortune is with them: their own corrupt beliefs and deeds cause it.
rows.anchor: سبب شؤمكم معكم وهو سوء عقيدتكم وأعمالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads ṭayrukum, using the form ṭayr instead of ṭāʾir.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «طيركم معكم»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhukkirtum means “when you were admonished”; the omitted response may be “you took it as an ill omen” or “you threatened to stone and punish us.”
rows.anchor: وعظتم، وجواب الشرط محذوف مثل تطيرتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reported readings place an alif between the hamzas, open the hamza of an to mean “Have you taken this as an omen because you were admonished?”, omit the interrogative, or read ayn dhukkirtum, meaning “your omen is with you wherever you are mentioned.”
rows.anchor: وقد قرىء بألف بين الهمزتين وبفتح أن بمعنى أتطيرتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They habitually exceed bounds in sin, which brings their misfortune, or in error, which explains their threats and suspicion toward those who deserve honor.
rows.anchor: قوم عادتكم الإسراف في العصيان فمن ثم جاءكم الشؤم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means “do not let their words grieve you.”
rows.anchor: فلا يهمنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant has the yāʾ with ḍamma, from aḥzana.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بضم الياء من أحزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their words may be blasphemy and association about God, or denial and disparagement directed at the Prophet.
rows.anchor: في الله بالإلحاد والشرك، أو فيك بالتكذيب والتهجين

words: إِنَّا نَعْلَمُ مَا يُسِرُّونَ وَمَا يُعْلِنُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows their private and public acts and will requite them; this knowledge consoles the Prophet and explains the prohibition.
rows.anchor: فنجازيهم عليه وكفى ذلك أن تتسلى به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause can be read anna with fatḥa, understood after deletion of the lām of purpose.
rows.anchor: على حذف لام التعليل جاز

words: أَوَلَمْ يَرَ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ أَنَّا خَلَقْنَٰهُ مِن نُّطْفَةٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder of humanity's creation from a drop is a second consolation; denial of resurrection is especially ugly since it denies God's power over what is easier than the first creation and repays an immense gift with disobedience.
rows.anchor: تسلية ثانية بتهوين ما يقولونه بالنسبة إلى إنكارهم الحشر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In the reported encounter, Ubayy ibn Khalaf brought the Prophet a decayed bone and crumbled it, asking whether God could revive it; the Prophet answered yes, saying He would raise Ubayy and cast him into Hell, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor:
فقال عليه الصلاة والسلام:
" نعم ويبعثك ويدخلك النار فنزلت "

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that, after being contemptible fluid, a person becomes distinct, articulate, and capable of arguing about what is within him.
rows.anchor: فإذا هو بعد ما كان ماء مهينا مميز منطيق قادر على الخصام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man advances an astonishing claim denying the power to resurrect the dead, or compares resurrection with what humans cannot do and describes God as unable.
rows.anchor: أمرا عجيبا وهو نفي القدرة على إحياء الموتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He forgets that God created him in the first place.
rows.anchor: خلقنا إياه

words: قَالَ مَن يُحْىِ ٱلْعِظَٰمَ وَهِىَ رَمِيمٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ramīm means decayed bones; the form may be active or passive participle, and it lacks feminine marking because it became a fixed noun.
rows.anchor: والرميم ما بلي من العظام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse indicates that bones possess life and are affected by death like the other bodily members.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على أن العظم ذو حياة فيؤثر فيه الموت كسائر الأعضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who originated the bones the first time will revive them; God's capacity has not changed, and the underlying matter remains receptive by its nature.
rows.anchor: فإن قدرته كما كانت لامتناع التغير فيه والمادة على حالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows every created thing in detail, including the origins, divisions, locations, and means of identifying scattered fragments, and how to reassemble them as before and restore their qualities or equivalents.
rows.anchor: يعلم تفاصيل المخلوقات بعلمه وكيفية خلقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are astonished that a warner came from among them, either a human like them or an unlettered member of their own people.
rows.anchor: بشر مثلهم أو أمي من عدادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them “the unbelievers” instead of using a pronoun rebukes them and signals that their disbelief emboldened this statement.
rows.anchor: وضع فيه الظاهر موضع الضمير غضبا عليهم وذما لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call the miracle he displays magic and his claims about God lies.
rows.anchor: فيما يظهره معجزة. { كذاب } فيما يقوله على الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They object that the many gods have been reduced to one deity; to them this conflicts with ancestral consensus and the apparent inability of one to know and control many things.
rows.anchor: بأن جعل الألوهية التي كانت لهم لواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adjective is also read with gemination, which intensifies the sense of astonishing, as in the intensified form karām.
rows.anchor: وقرىء مشددا وهو أبلغ ككرام وكرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After ʿUmar accepted Islam, Quraysh were distressed and appealed to Abū Ṭālib to settle matters with his nephew. The Prophet asked what they wanted; they demanded he abandon them and their idols, offering to leave him and his God alone.
rows.anchor: لما أسلم عمر رضي الله عنه شق ذلك على قريش

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet offered the Quraysh a single formula that would make Arabs submit to them and non-Arabs pay them tribute; when they agreed, he told them to say “There is no god but God,” and they got up and left.
rows.anchor: أرأيتم إن أعطيتكم ما سألتم أمعطي أنتم كلمة واحدة تملكون بها العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh's leading men left Abū Ṭālib's gathering after the Prophet had silenced them.
rows.anchor: وانطلق أشراف قريش من مجلس أبي طالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An is explanatory because leaving a discussion signals speech; alternatively, inṭilāq means launching into speech itself.
rows.anchor: هي المفسرة لأن الانطلاق عن مجلس التقاول يشعر بالقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of imshū is “gather together,” like the term for a woman having many children and the word for livestock.
rows.anchor: من مشت المرأة إذا كثرت أولادها ومنه الماشية أي اجتمعوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is also read without an, or with yamshūna an iṣbirū.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بغير { أن } وقرىء «يمشون أن اصبروا»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The leaders urge one another to remain firm in worshipping their gods, since talking with Muhammad will not help them.
rows.anchor: على عبادتها فلا ينفعكم مكالمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may mean that an unavoidable twist of fate is being directed against them; that monotheism or Muhammad's bid for leadership is something everyone desires; or that their religion is being targeted for seizure.
rows.anchor: إن هذا الأمر لشيء من ريب الزمان يراد بنا فلا مرد له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They mean the doctrine of one God that Muhammad teaches.
rows.anchor: بالذي يقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may mean the inherited religion in which their ancestors lived, or the last prior religion, Christianity, whose adherents teach a Trinity; alternatively it describes a prospective religion in which neither scriptural scholars nor soothsayers heard of monotheism.
rows.anchor: في الملة التي أدركنا عليها آباءنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call the claim a fabrication.
rows.anchor: كذب اختلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They resent the Qur'an being revealed to Muhammad when he is their equal or lower in social rank; like 43:31, their denial stems from envy and narrow concern for worldly status.
rows.anchor: إنكار لاختصاصه بالوحي وهو مثلهم أو أدون منهم في الشرف والرئاسة

words: بَلْ هُمْ فِى شَكٍّۢ مِّن ذِكْرِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They doubt the Qur'an or revelation because they cling to imitation and turn from proof; they do not hold a settled belief behind their claims that it is magic or fabrication.
rows.anchor: من القرآن أو الوحي لميلهم إلى التقليد وإعراضهم عن الدليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They have not yet tasted God's punishment; when forced to taste it, their doubt will end, since they will not believe until punishment compels them.
rows.anchor: بل لم يذوقوا عذابي بعد فإذا ذاقوه زال شكهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sends the rain into the ground as springs and channels, or makes waters spring up there; yanābīʿ can mean a water source or the water that gushes from it, parsed as location or state.
rows.anchor: هي عيون ومجاري كائنة فيها، أو مياه نابعات فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The crop's different colors may mean distinct species, such as wheat and barley, or varying hues such as green and red.
rows.anchor: أصنافه من بر وشعير وغيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The crop dries completely, at which point it is ready to break away from its place of growth; it then yellows and crumbles.
rows.anchor: يتم جفافه لأنه إذا تم جفافه حان له أن يثور عن منبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scene reminds observers either that a wise maker arranged it or that worldly life resembles this crop and should not deceive them; only people of understanding take the lesson.
rows.anchor: أو بأنه مثل الحياة الدنيا فلا تغتر بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has made such a person receptive to Islam with ease, creating a strong readiness to accept it without resistance; the chest houses the heart and the soul's receptivity.
rows.anchor: حتى تمكن فيه بيسر عبر به عمن خلق نفسه شديدة الاستعداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light is knowledge and guidance to the truth.
rows.anchor: يعني المعرفة والاهتداء إلى الحق

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says that when light enters the heart it expands; its sign is turning toward the eternal home, renouncing the deceptive world, and preparing for death before it arrives.
rows.anchor: إذا دخل النور القلب انشرح وانفسح، فقيل فما علامة ذلك

words: فَوَيْلٌۭ لِّلْقَٰسِيَةِ قُلُوبُهُم مِّن ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The predicate of man is omitted and supplied by the following warning. Min means “because of God's remembrance,” stronger than “away from it”: hardness caused by the reminder is greater refusal than hardness for another cause.
rows.anchor: من أجل ذكره وهو أبلغ من أن يكون عن مكان من

words: فَوَيْلٌۭ لِّلْقَٰسِيَةِ قُلُوبُهُم مِّن ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast magnifies the receptive and the resistant: God is said to open the first person's chest, while the second's hard heart is attributed to the person himself.
rows.anchor: وأسنده إلى الله وقابله بقساوة القلب وأسنده إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their error is manifest to anyone who gives it even a brief look.
rows.anchor: يظهر للناظر بأدنى نظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about Ḥamza, ʿAlī, Abū Lahab, and his son.
rows.anchor: والآية نزلت في حمزة وعلي وأبي لهب وولده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “best discourse” is the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: يعني القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Companions had grown weary and asked the Prophet to tell them something; this verse was then revealed.
rows.anchor: روي أن أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ملوا ملة فقالوا له حدثنا فنزلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beginning with God's name and construing the verb as directly as possible emphasizes the attribution to Him, magnifies the revelation, and attests to its excellence.
rows.anchor: وفي الابتداء باسم الله وبناء نزل عليه تأكيد للإسناد إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kitāban may be an appositive for aḥsan al-ḥadīth or a circumstantial accusative; the Qur'an's parts resemble each other in inimitability, responsive arrangement, sound meaning, and universal benefits.
rows.anchor: أو حال منه، وتشابهه تشابه أبعاضه في الإعجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathānī is the plural of mathnā, muthannā, or muthann, as discussed in Sūrat al-Ḥijr; it can describe the book through its constituent parts, like calling a person bones, veins, and nerves, or function as a specification of mutashābihan.
rows.anchor: جمع مثنى أو مثنى أو مثن على ما مر في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative construction makes mathānī a specification of mutashābihan, as in the phrase “a man whose qualities are beautiful.”
rows.anchor: أو جعل تمييزا من { متشبها } كقولك:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who fear God shudder from the warnings; the skin's contraction is an image of intense fear.
rows.anchor: تشمئز خوفا مما فيه من الوعيد، وهو مثل في شدة الخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is built from q-sh-ʿ, the name for dry leather, with an added rāʾ to make a quadriliteral, as aqmaṭarra is built from qamaṭa, “to tie.”
rows.anchor: وتركيبه من حروف القشع وهو الأديم اليابس بزيادة الراء

words: ثُمَّ تَلِينُ جُلُودُهُمْ وَقُلُوبُهُمْ إِلَىٰ ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their skins and hearts soften through mercy and encompassing forgiveness; the unqualified wording suggests that mercy is God's fundamental way and precedes wrath.
rows.anchor: بالرحمة وعموم المغفرة، والإطلاق للإشعار بأن أصل أمره الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition ilā incorporates the sense of settling and becoming tranquil; hearts are mentioned because fear is a condition of the heart.
rows.anchor: والتعدية ب { إلى } لتضمين معنى السكون والاطمئنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhālika may refer to the Qur'an itself or to the state of fear followed by hope.
rows.anchor: { ذلك } أي الكتاب أو الكائن من الخشية والرجاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guides whomever He wills to guide.
rows.anchor: يهدى به من يشاء } هدايته

words: وَمَن يُضْلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِنْ هَادٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever God abandons to error has no guide who can take him out of it.
rows.anchor: فما له من هاد
